_comment: The shared spaces: one Cyberplex collaboration project each. Exactly one owner per space. readers is a list of agents, or "*" for every agent listed under agents. decision_requesters may ask the tenant owner for a decision in that space. Project ids are NOT here: they go in spaces.local.json at the repository root (git-ignored). Read by server/proxy/proxy.py; agents never pass a project id. guide: what belongs in the document; agents get it from spaces_list and space_read. dispatchers: script agents allowed to call waiting_by_agent.

virtual-cto.description: Chief technology officer of the team. Owns the roadmap and the owner desk.

program-manager.description: Engineering program manager. Owns the work queue and turns approved work into tasks.

architect.description: Principal architect. Owns the technology baseline and the tech-debt list.

eng-director.description: Director of engineering. Reports on delivery.

security-lead.description: Head of security and reliability. Owns the risk register.

operations-manager.description: Operations manager. Owns the operations log.

finops-lead.description: FinOps manager. Owns the spend document.

owner-desk.title: Owner desk
owner-desk.objective: What the tenant owner has asked of the team, what the team is asking the owner, and where things stand in a few lines. The owner's directions are the accepted entries.
owner-desk.guide: One entry per open item between the team and the tenant owner: what was asked, by whom, and where it stands. Questions: what the team needs answered. The owner's directions are the accepted entries; do not restate them. Keep it under 15 entries and remove an item when it is closed.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.objective: Goals, milestones and their dates; what is planned next and why.
roadmap.guide: One entry per milestone: its name, target date, state (on track, at risk, late, done) and the one thing it depends on. Constraints: fixed dates and limits. No task-level detail.

work-queue.title: Work queue
work-queue.objective: Approved work: what is in progress, who has it, and what is blocked. Work is handed over as tasks addressed to a role.
work-queue.guide: One entry per approved work item in progress: record id, who has it, its state, and the blocker if any. Hand work over as tasks, not entries. Remove an entry when the work is verified done.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.objective: The technology baseline, the tech-debt list and the architecture decisions in force.
architecture.guide: The baseline in a few facts (runtime, data store, deploy path); each architecture decision in force with its ADR number; each tech-debt item with severity and next step.

risk-register.title: Risk register
risk-register.objective: Open risks and vulnerabilities, each with an owner and a next step.
risk-register.guide: One entry per open risk: what could happen, severity (low, medium, high, critical), the evidence, the owning role, and the next step with a date. Remove it when closed. Never record a secret or exploit detail.

operations.title: Operations
operations.objective: The running state of the service: outages, sign-ups, and mail that needs an answer.
operations.guide: The service state (up, degraded or down, and since when); open incidents; sign-ups awaiting action; mail awaiting an answer. Counts and states only, no personal data.

finance.title: Finance
finance.objective: Spend against budget and anything unusual.
finance.guide: Month-to-date spend against budget; each line over budget; each anomaly with its amount and suspected cause. Numbers come from the spend ledger.

collab-test.title: Collaboration test
collab-test.objective: A space for testing the collab-space tool. Nothing in it is real work. Safe to ignore.
collab-test.guide: A test space. Anything may be written here; nothing in it is real work.
